newsitem.title: INDIA: World Bank to fund 400 bln rupee India development.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to fund 400 bln rupee India development.

text.p: The World Bank will give India 400 billion rupees ($11.17 billion) over the next three years to finance infrastructure development projects, the United News of India (UNI) said on Tuesday.

UNI quoted the World Bank's India director, Edwin Lim, as saying the funds would be sanctioned for power projects, highway upgradation, poverty alleviation programmes and other infrastructure development projects.
Analysts say India needs to invest about $200 billion in infrastructure in the next five years to support a double-digit industrial growth rate.
They say the demand for power currently outstrips supply by 147,000 megawatts, and India needs investment worth more than $150 billion over the next 10 years to bridge the gap.
Upgrading roads and highways will require about $96 billion, the Ministry of Surface Transport says.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted Lim as saying the bank had initiated discussions for a 50 billion rupee to 70 billion rupee project-specific lending programme in the western desert state of Rajasthan.

The projects include a 10 billion rupee project to improve power transmission and distribution, a 19.7 billion rupee water and sewage project for five major towns, and a 7.4 billion rupee highway project, PTI said. ($1=35.8 rupees)
